title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — absolute 'death' ≠ corruption; tip before all-are-sinners proof
pass_a_gloss: Then you make Paul, against his custom, with 'death' set absolutely and with no addition, mean such corruption—and one and the same name, set once, to be taken once, yet both properly and figuratively at once. Besides, who believes death, when distinguished from sin as here, signifies sin? Tip before the all-are-sinners proof.
pass_b_english: Then you will bring in the Apostle against his custom, with the name of death set absolutely, and without any addition, signifying corruption of that kind, and one and the same name set once, to be understood once, taking it at once properly and figuratively. Besides, who would believe that death, when it is distinguished from sin, as is done in this place, signifies sin?
source_text: Tum Apostolum induces contra suum morem nomine mortis absolute posito, & sine ulla additione, eiusmodi corruptionem significantem, unumque & idem nomen semel positum, semel intelligendum, simul proprie & figurate accipientem. Praeterea, quis credat mortem cum a peccato distinguitur, ut fit hoc loco, peccatum significare?

choices.choice: Absolute death ≠ sin when distinguished; tip before all-sinners proof

notes: Cap. IX omit densify section 532 from locked 1661 Latin (pp. 329–330 tip).
